1225 East International Airport Road, Suite 200
                               Anchorage, Alaska 99518
                                   www.akaction.org

                                   November 2, 2026

Re: Docket Number P-15423, the Proposed DeepGreen Cook Inlet Underwater Data
Center

I am submitting these comments on behalf of Alaska Community Action on Toxics
(ACAT), a public interest, nonprofit, science-based environmental health research and
advocacy organization. ACAT has members who live, subsist, and recreate in the area
that would be directly and negatively affected by this proposed project.

We oppose the proposed DeepGreen Cook Inlet underwater data center to be sited in the
Forelands region near Nikiski, Alaska. Our concerns include: harm to the endangered
beluga whale such as noise interference, habitat fragmentation and disruption; heat
releases and warming water temperatures; toxic contamination such as copper and PFAS;
negative effects on local communities such as harm to salmon and salmon fisheries in
Cook Inlet, jobs and livelihoods of subsistence and commercial fishermen, as well as
energy and cost burdens on rate payers.

Data centers require the use of toxic chemicals such as PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl
substances). PFAS are highly toxic and associated with health harms at extremely low
exposure levels, including reproductive and developmental damage, certain cancers, and
immune system impairment. Trifluoroacetic acid, for example, is linked with endocrine
disruption of the thyroid and reproductive systems, liver toxicity, neuro- and
developmental toxicity, and adverse effects to the immune system. There is no health and
safety plan to address these public health concerns. Moreover, data centers generate large
quantities of hazardous waste including e-waste such as discarded microchips, electronic
equipment, and components. E-waste releases toxic chemicals into the environment and
downstream from landfills when disposed. The proposed DeepGreen data center would
also release copper. Copper is one of the most toxic elements to aquatic species including
salmon, at low levels just above those that are needed for growth and reproduction. It can
accumulate and cause irreversible harm to some species. Fish exposed to chronic and
sublethal levels of copper can suffer from impaired neurological and brain function,
 impaired reproduction; impaired predator detection and avoidance, impaired “homing”
ability and migration behaviors; and depressed immune response.

The proposed siting of the DeepGreen data center in Cook Inlet is reckless and
irresponsible. The Forelands is a narrow passage between upper and lower Cook Inlet.
The underwater data center in this area would disrupt fisheries and aquatic life, safe
passage of beluga whales, and ship traffic. Cook Inlet water is laden with glacial silt; and
in addition, experiences some of the largest tidal ranges in the world. Any infrastructure
exposed to its strong currents would face relentless, year-round abrasion, persistent wear,
and ongoing operational risks. Its infrastructure, made up of significant moving parts,
would require constant, difficult to access, maintenance, creating serious uncertainty
about long-term reliability and cost. Cook Inlet experiences frequent earthquakes, which
would shake and vibrate sensitive equipment like data center servers, causing damage
and requiring maintenance.

We request that FERC deny the permit for the DeepGreen Cook Inlet Underwater Data
Center. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,

Pamela Miller
Executive Director and Senior Scientist
